text:
marta: Quick sync — thinking about a new approach for the Dedicated warm pool. Current autoscaler reacts to intent tokens but we still hit cold-GPU tails for some model-heavy tenants. Idea: keep a tiny model-aware warm pool + packing rules instead of pure headroom credits.

kevin: clarifying q — by model-aware do you mean we track model affinities and keep GPUs with that model cached (KV+LLM weights) primed?

marta: yep. two signals: recent request pattern per model + tenant SLA tier. Forecasted active replicas -> convert to desired warm slots per model. Pack smaller models together where possible.

elaine: sounds good but packing introduces fragmentation risk. how do we handle mixed-precision/quantization incompatibilities?

marta: plan: prefer packing only when runtime-compatible (same quant config & sequence len profile). otherwise fall back to soft isolation. we keep a compatibility tag on each allocation.

santiago: how do we forecast? naive sliding window or ML predictor? also what window length? 5m for fast spikes, 1h for baseline?

marta: two-tier forecast: short-window (5m EWMA alpha=0.3) for immediate spikes, and a 1h seasonality baseline. desired_warm = max(short_pred * multiplier, baseline_pred * 0.6). multiplier depends on SLA.

ryan: multiplier by SLA is sensible. add safety floor for cold-start time: desired_warm >= ceil(cold_start_ms / avg_request_interval_ms). saves us from underprovisioning for slow spin-ups.

kevin: admission question — who owns the warm pool assignment? control-plane calculates desired_warm, operator implements allocation + packing, right?

marta: yes. control-plane emits an intent: {model, tenant, warm_slots, compatibility_tags, priority}. operator translates to actual VM/GPU assignments and placement constraints.

elaine: what about cost control? keeping warm GPUs around is expensive. maybe allow preemptible warm slots for lower-tier tenants and reserve non-preemptible for SLO-critical ones.

marta: agreed — plan: tiered warm class: guaranteed, best-effort, and preemptible. fallback policy: if guaranteed warm not available, degrade to best-effort; if that fails for high-SLA traffic, route to a lighter model variant (quantized) with a deprecation event.

santiago: rollout plan? We can A/B the predictor for a subset of tenants and measure tail latency and cost delta. Also add an observable: "warm_cache_hit_rate" per model + "packing_fragmentation_pct".

ryan: ops hooks: we need drain semantics so warm GPUs can be released without causing evictions that break KV caches mid-request. Add a grace window and mark eviction-safepoints in the operator.

kevin: small nit — when packing small models together, ensure KV cache privacy (no cross-tenant sharing). tenancy isolation must be preserved even on same GPU.

marta: yep isolation enforced at process level. packing only co-locates different tenants' processes but we keep separate address spaces and encryption keys.

elaine: on metrics, add predicted_vs_actual_warm_slots and a regression alert if warm cache hit falls below threshold for 10m.

ryan: experiment checklist: 1) implement intent API field warm_slots & tags, 2) operator packing + compatibility matcher, 3) short/long forecaster, 4) canary for 10 tenants (mix of SLA tiers), 5) dashboards + alerts.

santiago: I'll own the operator changes (packing/matching), ryan can own the drain semantics, marta you own the forecaster and control-plane intent, kevin + elaine pair on canary metrics and security review.

marta: thanks. ops-bot: create ticket template for the canary and auto-provision a test tenant list?

ops-bot: Created ticket #INF-6374 with checklist: forecaster impl, intent API, operator packing, canary tenant list, dashboards. Assignees: santiago, ryan, marta, kevin, elaine. ETA: 3 weeks. :white_check_mark:

kevin: one more thought — fallback routing to smaller quantized variant should be opt-in per tenant. we need a gating flag in tenant config.

marta: noted. we'll default to off and enable per-tenant in canary. Thanks all — I'll doc the intent schema and link the PR to the ticket.
